reading.body:
CyrusOne Austin, TX (AUS2-AUS3) in Austin, Texas, publishes 19 MW of IT capacity across 242,000 square feet of technical space, operated by CyrusOne.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1900 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 475 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

CyrusOne Austin, TX (AUS2-AUS3) holds 6 published certifications: PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), ISO 27001 (a certified information security management system), FISMA (a specific compliance or security standard), SSAE 16 Type II (a specific compliance or security standard), TIA-942 (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Texas has 23 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 15 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 399.41 MW. CyrusOne Austin, TX (AUS2-AUS3) contributes 19 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
